title: Categorical spin-networks: state-sum invariants of 4-manifolds from higher-gauge theory
authors: Hank Chen, Zhian Jia, Ran Luo, Wei Cui
abstract: In this work, we define $(3+1)$-dimensional topological quantum field theories (TQFTs) and their lattice realizations with input data given by a pivotal fusion 2-category; more precisely, our framework applies in wider generality to presemisimple locally fusion pivotal tensor $2$-categories, which are equipped with a so-called \textit{shadow trace}. We introduce a decoration of triangulated manifolds by the input data, and develop a $20j$-symbol formalism for computing 4-simplex scattering amplitudes. We verify the topological invariance of 20$j$-symbol summations under the 4-dimensional Pachner moves. Furthermore, we also construct explicitly a 3-dimensional Levin-Wen-type lattice Hamiltonian model realizing the state-sum invariant. Our construction can be understood as a higher-dimensional analogue of the spin-networks construction for the Turaev-Viro invariant. Examples arising from $2$-groups are discussed from the perspective of higher gauge theory.
summary: This paper develops a sophisticated mathematical framework to calculate topological invariants for 4-manifolds by generalizing spin-network constructions using higher-gauge theory. It introduces a $20j$-symbol formalism and constructs a corresponding 3D lattice Hamiltonian model. This work advances the understanding of TQFTs by connecting them to advanced categorical structures.
main_problem: The work aims to define and compute state-sum invariants for 4-manifolds using the framework of higher-gauge theory.
main_result: The authors develop a $20j$-symbol formalism that computes these invariants and construct an explicit 3D Levin-Wen-type lattice Hamiltonian model realizing the state-sum invariant.
method: The methodology involves decorating triangulated manifolds with input data from a presemisimple locally fusion pivotal tensor 2-category, leading to a higher-categorical analogue of spin-network constructions.
model_or_system: The theoretical framework models $(3+1)$-dimensional Topological Quantum Field Theories (TQFTs) and their lattice realizations, drawing parallels to the Turaev-Viro invariant and 4D Yetter-Dijkgraaf-Witten theory.
key_observables: State-sum invariants of 4-manifolds ($Z_C pM^4$), $20j$-symbols, and the resulting lattice Hamiltonian.
important_parameters: The input data is governed by a pivotal fusion 2-category equipped with a shadow trace.
main_assumptions: The framework requires the input 2-category $C$ to be 'sufficiently good' and relies on the mathematical structure of higher-gauge theory.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes; the notes mention Table 1 describing the construction layout from higher-group gauge theories.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the TQFT framework using 2-categories, developing the $20j$-symbol formalism for 4-simplex amplitudes, proving topological invariance via Pachner moves, and concluding with the explicit construction of a 3D lattice Hamiltonian.
why_interesting: While highly abstract, the connection between lattice Hamiltonians (like Levin-Wen models) and topological invariants is fundamental to understanding quantum phases of matter, which is a core theme in condensed matter theory.
